title: Automated diagnostic method for sleep apnea and hypopnea using overnight airflow and oxygen saturation
author: Yu, Huang, et al.

steps.title: Collect patient data
steps.instruction: Retrospectively collect data from 143 patients (122 males, 21 females, mean age 40.8 years) who presented with snoring or daytime sleepiness between July 1 2019 and October 30 2019 at the Eye & ENT Hospital of Fudan University, then anonymize all data for the entire analysis.

steps.title: Export PSG recordings
steps.instruction: Obtain overnight airflow and SpO₂ recordings from the clinical PSG system (Embla N7000, Natus, USA) and export the raw data files.

steps.title: Store time‑series data
steps.instruction: Save the airflow signal as a time series with 0.005‑s intervals (200 Hz sampling) and the SpO₂ signal as a time series with 0.1‑s intervals (10 Hz sampling). Also collect sleep‑monitoring data (sampling 1/30 Hz), manually marked SAH events (by five clinicians), event durations, and clinical AHI reports for later analysis.

steps.title: Divide cohort into groups
steps.instruction: Randomly assign the 143 patients to a training group of 100 individuals and a test group of 40 individuals (the remaining 3 patients are not used).

steps.title: Optimize detection parameters
steps.instruction: Use the training group to determine the optimal parameters for the automated procedure that detects SAH events.

steps.title: Test automated detection
steps.instruction: Apply the optimized automated procedure to the test group to evaluate its performance.

steps.title: Perform error analysis
steps.instruction: Conduct event‑by‑event error analysis comparing automated results with manual markings, classifying errors as (1) overcheck (false positive) when a non‑event is detected, or (2) miss (false negative) when an actual SAH event is not detected.

steps.title: Compute statistical metrics
steps.instruction: Compare AHI (SAH events per hour), apnea/hypopnea events per hour, etc., between automated and manual results; calculate the root‑mean‑square error (RMSE) using RMSE = √[ Σ_i=1^N (X_i^automate – X_i^manual)² / N ], where N is the number of patients.

steps.title: Run analysis on workstation
steps.instruction: Execute all analyses on a personal laptop equipped with an Intel i7‑8650U CPU and 16 GB RAM, using MATLAB R2020a; note that processing each patient’s raw ASCII data file (≈90–100 MB) takes under 3 seconds.
